notes: START AND THE 1804 PROCLAMATION. The page dates the empire to 'Proclamation: 11 August 1804' (Francis I), but Cliopatria's row begins in 1806 and the habsburg-monarchy dossier (another batch) closes in December 1805 and hands its land to this one, so the dossier starts in 1806 (found event at confidence 1) to avoid drawing 1804-1805 twice. END: 30 March 1867 (infobox) while Cliopatria's last shape runs to 1867 and its Austria-Hungary row starts in 1868. WHAT WAS CORRECTED. (1) 1809: the shape holds before the Treaty of Schönbrunn; a new 1810 keyframe uses the 1811 outline. (2) 1848: Lombardy-Venetia is a contest zone, not lost land. (3) 1849-1852: Cliopatria's 423,099 km2 leaves out Hungary, Slovakia, Transylvania and the Banat (1,055 cells); the 1853 outline is applied; the Hungarian zone is contested from December 1848 to 13 August 1849 with Cliopatria's 'Hungarian Nationalists' row (1849-1957, Q28513 = Austria-Hungary's Wikidata id) as counterpart, which is mis-dated; the Hungarian state of 1849 (Kossuth's Declaration of Independence, April 1849) has no dossier of its own. (4) 1856: the 438 extra cells are the Danubian Principalities, an occupation that began in 1854 (Crimean War page, 'for the duration of the war') not annexed land. (5) 1866-1867: Cliopatria drops 220 Czech cells for no reason on any page and keeps Venetia; corrected. UNVERIFIED (page budget, nine pages): 1806 (Pressburg is not itemised on any page opened), 1814 (the Illyrian and Italian occupation before the Final Act), 1820-1845 (identical outlines, no border change on the pages: the Austrian intervention in Naples and Piedmont of 1821, Romagna and Modena of 1831 and the Polish crisis of 1830-1831 are not on the pages), 1846 (Kraków: confidence 1, the year is Cliopatria's), 1860-1863. The Berchtesgaden, Innviertel and Hausruckviertel cessions of 1809 are not on the Schönbrunn page; Bukovina's 1850 split and the Voivodeship of Serbia and the Banat (1849-1860) are internal. The Second Schleswig War page says Prussia and Austria 'took over the respective administration of Schleswig and Holstein' (Gastein, 14 August 1865) without saying which administers which; Cliopatria's 1864-1865 shape draws Holstein (and no Schleswig) as Austrian. DISAGREEMENTS: the Final Act is 9 June 1815 (Congress page) and the Austrian Empire page gives 'Congress of Vienna: 8 June 1815'; the Treaty of Zürich is 11 November 1859 on the page, 10 November elsewhere; Magenta is 4 or 5 June 1859 on the same page; the area of 698,700 km2 has no year. The infobox area (698,700 km2) is 0.99 of Cliopatria's 691,307 km2 for 1815 and 0.86 of its 1856 peak (810,554). COUNTERPARTS: 'republic-of-san-marco' (Venice 1848-1849) and 'hungarian-nationalists' (Hungary 1849) need rebel dossiers; 'italian-republic' stands for the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy, 'republic-of-ragusa' (Cliopatria's row ends before 1815) and 'free-city-of-krakow' are other batches. GAZETTEER NAMES NEEDED: none beyond those the validator reports; Salzburg (region), Tyrol, Dalmatia, Holstein, Schleswig, Wallachia, Moldavia, Veneto/Mantova/Udine/Pordenone (Natural Earth regions and provinces) were resolved by the gazetteer. NOT COVERED: the 1848-1849 Hungarian Declaration of Independence date (the page says 'April 1849'), the Prussian occupation of Bohemia and Moravia in July 1866 (not on the page) and the Gastein division of Lauenburg. REPAIR 2026-11-01 (after the review of eu-20-d): (1) The 1814 keyframe is explained by occupation events with the neighbours' dates: Illyria 1813/10, Dalmatia 1813/12, Lombardy-Venetia 1814/4, a gain of Tyrol and Vorarlberg from Bavaria 1814/5 and of the left-bank Palatinate from the Empire 1814/4 (c1); the Final Act of 9 June 1815 ends the occupations and keeps the three gains as the formal title; Salzburg, the Innviertel and the bailiwick of Vils are dated 14 April 1816 (Treaty of Munich), the Palatinate goes to Bavaria the same day, and the Innviertel loss of 14 October 1809 is added. (2) 1848: Austria now records the loss of Lombardy (8 June) and Venice (5 July) and the regain (9 August) to agree with kingdom-of-sardinia; the contest events stay. (3) 1849: contest 20-23 March and occupation of Lomellina and Alessandria 24 March - 6 August added (zone also in the war). (4) Kraków: the annexation is 16 November 1846 (c3, Free City of Cracow page), the Austrian occupation 1836-1841 is added. (5) Added: Neapolitan War 1815 (event pair and war), Lauenburg 1865/8 (Gastein Convention), Bohemia as a contest zone 1866/6-7. (6) Not added: Duchy of Cieszyn (duchy-of-cieszyn /ledger/6-7, 1849) merges into Austrian Silesia, a crown land already inside the empire: no territory changes hands, so there is no gain or loss to mirror. (7) Disagreement kept: the empire's start stays 1806 although the page proclaims it on 11 August 1804 (see the found event).
